name: Dobot MG400 · StruderBot reference installation
summary: A Dobot MG400 desktop robotic arm fitted with a fixed-nozzle filament-extrusion end effector, programmed through tab-based DobotStudio Pro Lua.

modelConstraints.sourceNote: Axis count and motion primitives are confirmed by hands-on use of DobotStudio Pro's Lua API against this unit. Reach and rated payload are left null pending confirmation against Dobot's published MG400 datasheet — do not treat this manifest as a substitute for the manufacturer's own specification.

evidence.label: ROBOT-CONFIRMED
evidence.scope: Extensive planar print history on this installation across many milestone programs.

evidence.label: ROBOT-CONFIRMED
evidence.scope: Relay-controlled extrusion tool switched via a digital output; used throughout this installation's print history.

evidence.label: EXPERIMENTAL
evidence.scope: A shallow-slope (20°) non-planar cladding coupon printed successfully with clean surface quality. Steeper slopes are untested. Long, continuous coordinated-XYZ runs are a KNOWN limitation: layer-boundary transitions produced pauses and blobs that were not fully resolved as of the source project's last iteration.
evidence.reference: Migrated from the source project's non-planar cladding iteration notes; see docs/authoring/evidence-labels.md for what EXPERIMENTAL does and doesn't claim.

installedTooling.name: Fixed-nozzle filament extrusion end effector
installedTooling.description: Replaces the arm's default end effector. Adds mass and changes the fourth axis's tuned load, which is safety-relevant — see safetyNotes.

installedTooling.name: Remote-I/O button panel (reference pattern)
installedTooling.description: Two illuminated pushbuttons wired to digital inputs, with matching digital-output indicator lights, used for physical program selection instead of relying on the DobotStudio Pro script runner. See instanceConfiguration — which physical DI/DO channels this maps to is unit-specific wiring, not a universal fact about the MG400.

safetyNotes: A light desktop arm's axis servos are tuned for an expected end-effector mass. Swapping to a materially heavier or lighter tool than that tuning assumes can produce vibration or unstable motion — verify empirically at reduced speed before running unattended, and treat load/tuning changes as a safety-relevant event, not a cosmetic one.

Prefer the controller's remote-I/O / physical-button execution path over its interactive script runner for repeated or unattended runs; script-runner behavior was observed to be less consistent during calibration on this installation.

A frame (tool frame / user frame) edit may not take effect reliably until the controller connection is cycled. After any frame edit: save, reconnect or power-cycle, run a small axis-marker move, and only then attempt a full program.
Treat the physical motion and print result as ground truth over any live IDE coordinate readout or software preview.
